author: Gould, 1855

art.subject: Silver-throated Bushtit (Aegithalos glaucogularis), adult (sexes alike, plumage similar year-round): a whitish to pale buff stripe along the centre of the crown, bordered on each side by a broad black band running from above the eye to the nape; cheeks and sides of the neck pale greyish-white; a small dusky grey-black patch in the centre of the lower throat; back and rump grey; wings blackish with pale edges to the tertials; breast, belly and flanks washed pinkish-buff; very long black tail with white outer edges; tiny stubby black bill; dark eye; dark legs.
art.pose: clinging to a thin twig, side view, long tail held straight
art.scene: bare deciduous shrubs at a woodland edge on a Korean offshore island in late autumn, soft daylight; no people, buildings or text
art.build: A tiny, round-bodied tit with a very long, narrow, graduated tail that is longer than the body, shaped exactly like the Long-tailed Tit of Korea. Body about the size of a Japanese White-eye's, the tail making the bird look much longer. Round head with no crest and almost no visible neck. Bill very short, stubby and triangular. Short dark legs; clings to and hangs from thin twigs. Wings short and rounded, reaching only the base of the tail. In flight a small ball trailing a long thin tail; moves in small restless flocks.
avoid: Do not paint an all-white head; this species has broad black bands along the sides of the crown.
Do not omit the small dark throat patch; the Long-tailed Tit (Aegithalos caudatus) of Korea has a clean white throat.
Do not make the underparts clean white; they are washed pinkish-buff.
Do not give it a long or thin bill; it is tiny and stubby.
